arguments.summary:
Fixed Pocket Notes draft persistence. The root cause was in src/storage.js: readDraft() always returned an empty draft and writeDraft/clearDraft were no-ops, so any unfinished draft was lost when switching between the Draft and My notes screens or refreshing the page.

Change (src/storage.js only): implemented the draft storage layer using the existing localStorage-based storage module (same `pocket-notes:` prefix, keyed by pathname). readDraft() now returns the stored draft or { title: '', body: '' }; writeDraft() persists the draft; clearDraft() removes it. No changes to src/app.js were needed — it already calls writeDraft on every input and reads the draft on each render, so the draft now survives tab switches and page refreshes. Saving still creates exactly one note (with a randomUUID id, keeping notes distinct), clears the draft, and prepends to existing notes, which are preserved. Appearance, data-testid attributes, and escaping behavior are untouched.

Verification: ran the protected browser acceptance suite — all 6 checks pass, including "Draft survives switching screens" and "Draft survives page refresh" (previously failing), plus save/clear/preserve/distinct behavior. Drafts and notes are stored as plain text (JSON-stringified), not interpreted HTML.

summary:
Fixed Pocket Notes draft persistence. The root cause was in src/storage.js: readDraft() always returned an empty draft and writeDraft/clearDraft were no-ops, so any unfinished draft was lost when switching between the Draft and My notes screens or refreshing the page.

Change (src/storage.js only): implemented the draft storage layer using the existing localStorage-based storage module (same `pocket-notes:` prefix, keyed by pathname). readDraft() now returns the stored draft or { title: '', body: '' }; writeDraft() persists the draft; clearDraft() removes it. No changes to src/app.js were needed — it already calls writeDraft on every input and reads the draft on each render, so the draft now survives tab switches and page refreshes. Saving still creates exactly one note (with a randomUUID id, keeping notes distinct), clears the draft, and prepends to existing notes, which are preserved. Appearance, data-testid attributes, and escaping behavior are untouched.

Verification: ran the protected browser acceptance suite — all 6 checks pass, including "Draft survives switching screens" and "Draft survives page refresh" (previously failing), plus save/clear/preserve/distinct behavior. Drafts and notes are stored as plain text (JSON-stringified), not interpreted HTML.
